name: Carlos Kleiber
milestone_by_age_26: Made his professional conducting debut in 1954 at age 24 with the operetta Gasparone at the Potsdam theatre, after serving as a repetiteur at the Gartnerplatz Theatre in Munich from 1952.
early_history_summary: Born in Berlin to the eminent conductor Erich Kleiber and an American mother, Carlos grew up in Buenos Aires after the family emigrated in 1935. His father actively discouraged him from pursuing music, so Carlos first studied chemistry at ETH Zurich before switching to music around age 20. He became a repetiteur at the Gartnerplatz Theatre in Munich in 1952 and made his conducting debut in Potsdam in 1954.
family_context_summary: Son of Erich Kleiber, one of the world's leading conductors, and American Ruth Goodrich. The family emigrated from Nazi Germany to Buenos Aires in 1935. Carlos grew up in a wealthy, culturally elite household with English boarding schools.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Erich Kleiber was an internationally renowned conductor who conducted the Berlin Staatsoper and the world premiere of Berg's Wozzeck. Despite actively discouraging Carlos from music, the household was deeply immersed in classical music at the highest level.
primary_early_advantage_tags: conductor father, musical household, elite cultural milieu, father discouragement as catalyst
evidence_summary: Carlos Kleiber was born into one of classical music's most elite families: his father Erich Kleiber was a world-famous conductor. Despite his father's active discouragement, Carlos grew up immersed in the highest levels of operatic and orchestral culture. He studied chemistry first, then switched to music around age 20, quickly securing repetiteur positions in Munich and making his conducting debut at 24. The family's wealth and cultural connections provided a platform, though his father's opposition may have created an independent drive.
starting_point: Born in Berlin in 1930 to the eminent Austrian conductor Erich Kleiber and American mother Ruth Goodrich; family emigrated to Buenos Aires in 1935 to escape Nazi Germany, raised in a wealthy, culturally elite household.
current_position: Died in 2004 at age 74 in Konjšica, Slovenia; widely regarded as among the greatest conductors of all time, known for his perfectionism and infrequent but legendary performances.

trajectory.event: Became a repetiteur at the Gartnerplatz Theatre in Munich, entering the professional musical world.
Made his conducting debut with the operetta Gasparone at the Potsdam theatre under the pseudonym Karl Keller.
Appointed Kapellmeister at the Deutsche Oper am Rhein in Dusseldorf and Duisburg, his first major conducting post.
Made his British debut conducting Wozzeck at the Edinburgh Festival, the opera his father had premiered in 1925.
Made his Bayreuth Festival debut conducting Tristan und Isolde, cementing his international reputation.
Made his American debut with the Chicago Symphony Orchestra, his only US orchestra appearances.
Made his Metropolitan Opera debut conducting La Boheme in New York.
Died on July 13, 2004, in Konjšica, Slovenia, leaving a legendary but sparse recorded legacy.

name: Zhuang Zedong
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first World Table Tennis Championship men's singles title in 1961 at age 21, the first of three consecutive world singles championships (1961, 1963, 1965).
early_history_summary: Born in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province, Zhuang started playing table tennis at age 10 and joined the Beijing Children's Palace amateur sports school at 14. He won the mixed doubles title at the 1957 national championships and was selected for the Chinese national team. In 1959, he won the men's singles at the Scandinavian International Championships, establishing himself internationally before his World Championship breakthrough in 1961.
family_context_summary: Born in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province, China. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources beyond his place of birth and early involvement in table tennis.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chinese national team pipeline, early specialization, Beijing Children's Palace, coach Fu Qifang, table tennis as national sport
evidence_summary: Zhuang Zedong began playing table tennis at age 10 in China and joined the Beijing Children's Palace sports school at 14, entering the Chinese national table tennis pipeline at a time when table tennis was declared China's national sport by Mao. He progressed rapidly through the national system, winning the national mixed doubles title at 17 and the Scandinavian International at 19, before becoming world champion at 21. The Chinese national sports system provided elite training, coaching from Fu Qifang, and intense competitive immersion from a young age.
starting_point: Born in 1940 in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province, China; family background not documented in reviewed sources; began playing table tennis at age 10.
current_position: Died on February 10, 2013, at age 72 in Beijing; remembered as a three-time world table tennis champion and key figure in ping-pong diplomacy between China and the United States.

trajectory.event: Won the mixed doubles title at the Chinese national table tennis championships, marking his emergence on the national scene.
Won the men's singles championship at the Scandinavian International Table Tennis Championships, his first major international title.
Won his first World Table Tennis Championship men's singles title in Beijing, becoming China's first world singles champion.
Won his second consecutive World Championship men's singles title in Prague.
Won his third consecutive World Championship men's singles title in Ljubljana, achieving an unprecedented three-peat.
Initiated ping-pong diplomacy by engaging with American player Glenn Cowan at the 31st World Championships in Nagoya, helping thaw Sino-American relations.
Appointed Director of China's National Sports Commission, entering national politics during the Cultural Revolution.
Died on February 10, 2013, in Beijing after a battle with cancer.

name: Thomas Muster
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first ATP top-level tournament at the Dutch Open in Hilversum in 1986 at age 18, defeating Jakob Hlasek in straight sets.
early_history_summary: Born in Leibnitz, Austria, Muster attended the Sports Boarding School in Suedstadt, Vienna, where he developed his tennis game. He first came to prominence by reaching the final of the French Open junior tournament and the Orange Bowl in 1985. He turned professional in 1985 and won his first ATP title at the Dutch Open in 1986 at age 18, establishing himself as a rising star on the professional tour.
family_context_summary: Born in Leibnitz, Styria, Austria. Family background beyond his birthplace is not documented in reviewed sources. He attended the Sports Boarding School in Suedstadt, Vienna, indicating some level of institutional support for his athletic development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sports Boarding School Suedstadt, coach Ronnie Leitgeb, early junior success, Austrian tennis system
evidence_summary: Thomas Muster grew up in Leibnitz, Austria, and attended the Sports Boarding School in Suedstadt, Vienna, which provided specialized athletic training. He reached the French Open junior final in 1985 and won his first ATP title at 18 in 1986. His coach Ronnie Leitgeb was a sustained mentor from 1984. Muster was known for his intense concentration and physical intensity, which became hallmarks of his clay-court dominance. No family financial or domain advantages are documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in 1967 in Leibnitz, Styria, Austria; attended the Sports Boarding School in Suedstadt, Vienna for specialized athletic training; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Former world No. 1 tennis player (February 1996), retired from professional tennis in 1999 with 44 ATP singles titles including the 1995 French Open; resides in Austria.

trajectory.event: Reached the final of the French Open junior tournament and the Orange Bowl, turning professional the same year.
Won his first ATP top-level tournament at the Dutch Open in Hilversum, defeating Jakob Hlasek in straight sets.
Suffered a severe knee injury when struck by a car at the Lipton International in Key Biscayne, threatening his career but demonstrating extraordinary determination to return.
Won the French Open singles title, becoming the first Austrian to win a Grand Slam singles tournament.
Reached the ATP world No. 1 singles ranking on February 12, 1996, cementing his status as the dominant clay-court player of the era.
Retired from professional tennis with 44 ATP singles titles and over $12 million in career prize money.

name: Maurizio Gucci

name: Aung San Suu Kyi
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found. By age 26 (1971), she had graduated from Oxford University (1968) and was working as an Assistant Secretary at the United Nations. Her rise to prominence came in 1988 at age 43 with the 8888 Uprising in Burma, and she won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1991 at age 46.
early_history_summary: Born in Rangoon, Burma, the daughter of Aung San, the assassinated independence hero of Burma. Her mother was appointed ambassador to India in 1960, and Suu Kyi completed schooling in New Delhi before studying at St Hugh's College, Oxford (1964-1968). She then worked at the United Nations in New York (1969-1971) before marrying Michael Aris in 1972.
family_context_summary: Daughter of General Aung San, the Father of Independent Burma, who was assassinated in 1947 when she was two. Her mother Daw Khin Kyi was a prominent diplomat appointed as Burma's ambassador to India in 1960.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was the founding father of independent Burma; mother was a prominent public figure and diplomat. The family held significant political legacy and status in Burma.

name: Ravindra Jadeja
milestone_by_age_26: Made his ODI debut for India on February 8, 2009 at age 20, scoring an unbeaten 60 against Sri Lanka. He was also vice-captain of the Indian team that won the 2008 U-19 Cricket World Cup at age 19.
early_history_summary: Born in Navagam Ghed, Gujarat, to a family of modest means, Jadeja joined the Nawanagar Cricket Academy in Jamnagar at age eight under coach Mahendrasinh Chauhan. He made his first Under-19 appearance for India in 2005 at age 16, played in the 2006 U-19 World Cup, and was vice-captain of the victorious Indian team at the 2008 U-19 World Cup. He made his ODI debut for India in February 2009 at age 20.
family_context_summary: Born to Lataben and Anirudhsinh Jadeja in a family of modest means in Gujarat. His mother was a nurse and the family lived in a one-room flat. His mother died in a kitchen accident when Jadeja was around 16, devastating him but also strengthening his resolve to pursue cricket.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family domain advantage in cricket is documented. His father wanted him to attend Sainik School for a military career, but Jadeja chose cricket.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early cricket academy, coach Chauhan, U-19 World Cup, Indian cricket system, modest background, mother's death as catalyst
evidence_summary: Ravindra Jadeja grew up in modest circumstances in Gujarat, joining the Nawanagar Cricket Academy at age eight under coach Mahendrasinh Chauhan, who emphasized fitness and fielding. He progressed through age-group cricket to the Indian U-19 team by 16, playing in two U-19 World Cups. His mother's death when he was 16 was a significant adversity that strengthened his determination. The Indian cricket system provided the performance pipeline, and the IPL era beginning in 2008 created a structural wave that accelerated his career. No family financial or domain advantages are documented.
starting_point: Born in 1988 in Navagam Ghed, Gujarat, India to a family of modest means; father was a security guard, mother a nurse; family lived in a one-room flat; joined Nawanagar Cricket Academy at age 8.
current_position: Active Indian international cricketer; one of India's premier all-rounders; plays for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL; has represented India in Tests, ODIs, and T20Is for over 15 years.

trajectory.event: Played in the ICC U-19 Cricket World Cup in Sri Lanka, taking three wickets in the final against Pakistan.
Served as vice-captain of the Indian team that won the 2008 U-19 Cricket World Cup, taking 10 wickets in six games.
Made his ODI debut for India against Sri Lanka on February 8, scoring an unbeaten 60.
Made his Test debut for India against England on December 13 in Nagpur.
Was part of the Indian team that won the ICC Champions Trophy, contributing significantly with the ball.
Played a key role in India's T20 World Cup campaign and continued as a premier all-rounder across all formats.

name: Szilveszter Csollány
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal on rings at the 1988 Junior European Championships in Avignon at age 18, and followed with a bronze at the 1990 senior European Championships at age 20, establishing himself as an international medalist on rings.
early_history_summary: Born in Sopron, Hungary, Csollány started gymnastics at age 5-6 in Gyor under coach Nandor Szolas. He moved to Budapest in 1986 to compete with Ujpest Dozsa. His first major success was fifth place at the 1986 European Youth Championships, and he won bronze on rings at the 1988 Junior European Championships. He joined the Hungarian senior national team in 1989 and won his first senior international medal (bronze on rings) at the 1990 European Championships.
family_context_summary: Born in Sopron, Hungary. His older brother's gymnastics training inspired him to try gymnastics at home, imitating his brother's movements. Family financial background is not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family domain advantage in gymnastics is documented. His brother's involvement in gymnastics provided early exposure to the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hungarian gymnastics system, early start at age 5, coach Nandor Szolas, extraordinary physical strength, Raba ETO club
evidence_summary: Szilveszter Csollány began gymnastics at age 5-6 in Gyor, Hungary, inspired by his older brother's training. He was coached by Nandor Szolas at Raba ETO and showed extraordinary physical strength from childhood. He moved to Budapest at 16 to join Ujpest Dozsa, entering the Hungarian national gymnastics pipeline. By 18, he won bronze at the Junior European Championships, and by 20, he earned a senior European Championship bronze on rings. The Hungarian gymnastics system provided the institutional framework for his development.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Sopron, Hungary; started gymnastics at age 5-6 in Gyor inspired by his older brother; family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died on January 24, 2022, at age 51 in Budapest, Hungary; Olympic gold medalist on rings (2000 Sydney) and World Champion (2002), remembered as one of Hungary's greatest gymnasts.

trajectory.event: Achieved fifth place on rings and pommel horse at the European Youth Championships, his first major international result.
Won bronze medal on rings at the Junior European Championships in Avignon, confirming his international potential.
Won bronze medal on rings at the senior European Championships, his first senior international podium.
Finished sixth on rings at the Barcelona Olympics and won silver on rings at the World Championships in Paris.
Won silver medal on rings at both the World Championships and the Atlanta Olympics, establishing himself as a world-class gymnast.
Won Olympic gold on rings at the Sydney Olympics with a score of 9.85, the pinnacle of his career.
Won gold on rings at the World Championships in Debrecen, Hungary, and was named Hungarian Sportsman of the Year.
Died on January 24, 2022, in Budapest after a long illness.

name: Albert Pujols
milestone_by_age_26: Made his MLB debut on April 2, 2001 at age 21 and was named the National League Rookie of the Year that season, after a dominant single minor-league season in 2000 where he was named Midwest League MVP.
early_history_summary: Born in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, Pujols was introduced to baseball by his father, a popular pitcher in the DR. The family immigrated to the United States when Albert was 16, settling in Independence, Missouri. He impressed scouts at Maple Woods Community College but was drafted only in the 13th round of the 1999 MLB draft. He spent one dominant season in the minors in 2000, winning Midwest League MVP, before making the Cardinals' Opening Day roster in 2001 and winning NL Rookie of the Year.
family_context_summary: Born in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. His father was a popular pitcher in the Dominican Republic who introduced him to baseball. The family immigrated to the United States when Albert was 16, eventually settling in Independence, Missouri. The family was not wealthy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a popular amateur pitcher in the Dominican Republic, providing early baseball exposure and instruction. However, the father did not play professionally at a high level.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father as baseball mentor, Dominican baseball culture, immigration to US, community college baseball, 13th round draft as motivation
evidence_summary: Albert Pujols grew up in the Dominican Republic, where his father, a popular amateur pitcher, introduced him to baseball. The family immigrated to the US when he was 16, settling in Missouri. Despite impressive play at Maple Woods Community College, he was drafted only in the 13th round due to concerns about his age and position. He used this as motivation, dominating the minor leagues in 2000 and making the Cardinals' Opening Day roster in 2001, winning NL Rookie of the Year. His path was marked by immigration challenges, low draft position, and self-driven improvement rather than inherited advantages.
starting_point: Born in 1980 in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic; father was a popular amateur pitcher who introduced him to baseball; family immigrated to the US when Albert was 16, settling in Independence, Missouri; family was not wealthy.
current_position: Retired MLB player after the 2022 season; 703 career home runs (4th all-time), 3,384 hits, three-time NL MVP, 11-time All-Star, two-time World Series champion; considered one of the greatest right-handed hitters in baseball history; future Hall of Famer.

trajectory.event: Dominated the minor leagues across three levels, winning Midwest League MVP with the Peoria Chiefs and Pacific Coast League postseason MVP with the Memphis Redbirds.

Won his first World Series championship with the St. Louis Cardinals.
Won his second World Series with the Cardinals before signing a 10-year contract with the Los Angeles Angels.
Hit his 700th career home run in his final MLB season, joining an exclusive club of only four players in history.

name: Waichiro Omura

He played at the Melbourne Olympics in November 1956 and also competed at the 1958 Asian Games, earning 5 caps for Japan between 1956 and 1958.

name: Wilbur Smith
milestone_by_age_26: No material independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found. By age 26 (1959), Smith was working as an accountant after graduating from Rhodes University. His first published novel, When the Lion Feeds, appeared in 1964 when he was 31. His first short story sale to Argosy magazine was in 1963 at age 30.
early_history_summary: Born in 1933 in Ndola, Northern Rhodesia (now Zambia), Smith grew up on his parents' 25,000-acre cattle ranch. He was educated at Michaelhouse and Rhodes University, initially wanting to be a journalist but persuaded by his father to study accountancy. He worked as an accountant and in his father's sheet metal factory before turning to writing in his late twenties.
family_context_summary: Born to Elfreda and Herbert Smith on a 25,000-acre cattle ranch in Northern Rhodesia. His mother loved books and read to him every night. His father was a ranch owner who later made bad investments, and had never read a book. Smith was named after aviator Wilbur Wright.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a book lover who instilled a reading habit in Smith from an early age. Father was a cattle rancher and later a metal factory worker. No direct literary or publishing family domain advantage.

name: Dieter Rams
milestone_by_age_26: Co-designed the Braun SK4 Phonosuper radiogram (known as 'Snow White's coffin') with Hans Gugelot in 1956 at age 24, a product considered revolutionary in industrial design, after joining Braun in 1955 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Wiesbaden, Germany, Rams began studying architecture and interior decoration at the Wiesbaden School of Art in 1947 at age 15. He took a break for a carpentry apprenticeship, then returned and graduated with honours in architecture in 1953. He worked for Frankfurt architect Otto Apel before joining Braun in 1955 at age 23, where he became a protege of Fritz Eichler and Ulm School of Design professors Hans Gugelot and Otl Aicher. He co-designed the iconic SK4 radiogram in 1956.
family_context_summary: Born in Wiesbaden, Germany. His godfather was a carpenter specializing in hand-polishing of surfaces, which provided early exposure to craftsmanship. Family financial background is not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Godfather was a carpenter who introduced Rams to craftsmanship and working with materials, providing early domain exposure to making and finishing objects.
primary_early_advantage_tags: carpentry apprenticeship, Wiesbaden School of Art, Hans Gugelot mentorship, Braun, Ulm School of Design, post-war German design renaissance
evidence_summary: Dieter Rams grew up in Wiesbaden, Germany, where his godfather, a carpenter, introduced him to craftsmanship. He began studying architecture at 15, completed a carpentry apprenticeship, and graduated with honours in 1953. He joined Braun in 1955 at 23 and immediately became a protege of Fritz Eichler and Ulm School of Design professors Hans Gugelot and Otl Aicher. Co-designing the revolutionary SK4 radiogram at 24 established him as a significant design talent. The post-war German design renaissance and the Braun-Ulm School collaboration provided a unique creative ecosystem.
starting_point: Born in 1932 in Wiesbaden, Germany; godfather was a carpenter who introduced him to craftsmanship; began studying architecture and interior decoration at age 15 at the Wiesbaden School of Art.
current_position: Retired German industrial designer, former head of design at Braun (1961-1997); widely regarded as one of the most influential industrial designers of the 20th century; his 'ten principles of good design' continue to shape design practice globally; resides in Kronberg im Taunus, Germany.

trajectory.event: Graduated in architecture with honours from the Wiesbaden School of Art and began working for Frankfurt architect Otto Apel.
Joined Braun as an architect and interior designer, beginning his lifelong association with the company.
Co-designed the Braun SK4 Phonosuper radiogram with Hans Gugelot, a revolutionary product known as 'Snow White's coffin' that became an icon of industrial design.
Became head of design at Braun, a position he would hold for 36 years until his retirement.
Retired from Braun after a 42-year career that produced some of the most influential product designs of the 20th century.
Received the Lifetime Achievement Medal at the London Design Festival, cementing his legacy as one of design's greatest figures.

name: Joaquín Cortés
milestone_by_age_26: Was accepted as a member of the prestigious Spanish National Ballet company in 1984 at approximately age 14-15, and became a principal soloist at age 16, performing at venues such as the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and the Kremlin Palace in Moscow.
early_history_summary: Born to a Gitano (Romani) family in Cordoba, Spain, Cortes showed interest in dancing from an early age and was encouraged by his uncle Cristobal Reyes, a successful flamenco dancer. His family moved to Madrid in 1981, where he began formal dance training at approximately age 12. By age 14, he was admitted to the Spanish National Ballet, and by 16 he became a principal soloist, touring the world with the company before leaving in 1988 to pursue an independent career.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class Gitano family in Cordoba, Spain. His father worked as a caterer in Malaga, and he was largely raised by his grandparents in a working-class neighborhood of Madrid. His uncle Cristobal Reyes was a successful flamenco dancer who helped him enter the National Ballet school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Uncle Cristobal Reyes was a successful flamenco dancer who had lived in London and knew Nureyev, providing direct domain mentorship and access to the professional dance world. The Gitano family heritage placed Cortes within the cultural tradition of flamenco.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Spanish National Ballet, uncle Cristobal Reyes, Gitano flamenco heritage, Madrid dance scene, early admission at 14, principal soloist at 16
evidence_summary: Joaquin Cortes was born into a working-class Gitano family in Cordoba and moved to Madrid at age 12, where his uncle Cristobal Reyes, a successful flamenco dancer, helped him gain entry to the Spanish National Ballet school. By 14, he was admitted to the Spanish National Ballet company, and by 16 he was a principal soloist performing at the Metropolitan Opera House and the Kremlin Palace. His Gitano heritage provided deep cultural immersion in flamenco, while the National Ballet provided elite institutional training. Despite modest financial circumstances, the combination of family mentorship, cultural heritage, and institutional access propelled his early career.
starting_point: Born in 1969 in Cordoba, Spain to a working-class Gitano family; father worked as a caterer in Malaga; raised largely by grandparents in a working-class Madrid neighborhood; uncle Cristobal Reyes was a successful flamenco dancer.
current_position: Active Spanish flamenco dancer and choreographer; runs his own company Joaquin Cortes Ballet Flamenco; considered one of the most famous flamenco dancers in the world; continues to perform and tour internationally.

trajectory.event: Accepted as a member of the prestigious Spanish National Ballet company, beginning his professional dance career as a teenager.
Became a principal soloist of the Spanish National Ballet, known for his phenomenal stamina and athleticism, performing at major venues worldwide.

Formed his own company, Joaquin Cortes Ballet Flamenco, and launched his first international tour 'Cibayi' at the Champs Elysees Theatre in Paris.
Launched 'Pasion Gitana' (Gypsy Passion), his most successful show, which toured over 30 countries and was seen by more than one million people.
Launched the 'Soul' tour across North and South America and was the subject of a documentary film.
